agent.problem: Moses and Aaron appear here for the first time, but neither is identified. The rest of the walkthrough also uses Moses' name without giving a simple introduction, leaving a new reader with names only.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

agent.problem: Cards 2, 6, 9, 11, 13 and 18 ask for details that cannot be reasoned out from anything in the earlier cards. That is six of the eleven choice cards, so discovery questions make up most of the stop instead of only a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The blank asks for "holy," the unseen wording of verse 40, and no preceding card establishes that result or gives a way to distinguish it from "useful" or "known." It tests unshown wording rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
